title: Deadlock
description: Learn about deadlocks and how they occur in SQL Server.

data.text: A deadlock is a concurrency problem where two sessions block each other's progress. Each session holds a lock on a resource the other session needs.
In a deadlock, SQL Server proactively terminates one of the sessions. The terminated session is called the deadlock victim.
Two sessions access the same tables in different orders:

rows: UPDATE invoices SET customer_id = 100 WHERE id = 1
UPDATE invoice_items SET amount = 100 WHERE id = 10
UPDATE invoice_items SET item_name = 'Cool Keyboard' WHERE id = 10 — Blocked
UPDATE invoices SET total = ... WHERE id = 1 — Blocked

data.caption: A deadlock cycle: each session holds one lock and waits for the other.
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    S1["Session 1\nholds lock on invoices row 1"] --> W1["Session 1 waits for\ninvoice_items row 10"]
    S2["Session 2\nholds lock on invoice_items row 10"] --> W2["Session 2 waits for\ninvoices row 1"]
    W1 --> S2
    W2 --> S1
    W1 --> D["SQL Server detects the cycle"]
    W2 --> D
    D --> V["One session is chosen\nas the deadlock victim (error 1205)"]

data.text: Open two query windows and run each script at the same time. Each transaction takes a lock first and then asks for the row the other transaction already holds, which forms a cycle.

data.title: Session 1
data.content: Locks the invoice first, then tries to update an invoice item.

data.title: Session 2
data.content: Locks the invoice item first, then tries to update the invoice.

data.title: Handling error 1205 in application code
data.text: The victim's transaction is rolled back and the client receives error 1205. Applications should catch that error and retry the whole transaction with a short randomized backoff. `SET DEADLOCK_PRIORITY LOW` on a background job makes it the preferred victim, but it does not prevent deadlocks — consistent access order does.

data.title: Deadlock Key Points
points: Deadlocks occur when two sessions lock resources the other needs.
SQL Server chooses one session as the deadlock victim.
Design applications to access tables in a consistent order to prevent deadlocks.
The deadlock victim receives an error message and must retry the transaction.
